tofu-base.note: Fixed pet tone; never relit by the clock.

onigiri-base.note: Fixed pet tone; never relit by the clock.

lantern-light.note: Toro window and dithered halo at night.

crumb-gold.note: Eat crumbs; the same gold is the alert ring and alert verb in the chrome.

display.purpose: Wordmark, notice titles, "get a pet", privacy headings. Zen Maru Gothic 500/700 only.

tag.purpose: Pet name on its name tag; verb follows in tag-verb at 75% opacity.

tag-verb.purpose: Lowercase state verb inside the tag.

command.purpose: Strings the visitor types or pastes; never names or headings.

shadows.name: chip-float
shadows.purpose: Every frosted chip, tag, pill, hint and notice. Paired with backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(1.3).

motion.name: tag-lift
motion.purpose: Tag hover/focus; uses translate/scale properties, not transform.

motion.name: sprite-rates
motion.value: idle 4f@3fps, eat 4f@5, wave 2f@4, work 2f@6, sleep 3f@1.5, cheer 4f@8; per-pet offset 1.7 frames
motion.purpose: Pet state loops; reduced motion holds frame 0.

motion.name: boop
motion.value: 0.45s sine hop up to 5px + 3 pixel hearts

motion.name: ripple
motion.purpose: Task finished, or pond tap (koi x3 speed for 0.9s).

motion.name: clouds
motion.purpose: Day sky; frozen with reduced motion.

motion.name: night-life
motion.value: stars twinkle, up to 9 fireflies, lantern flicker between two baked densities
motion.purpose: Night only; static with reduced motion.

motion.name: clock
motion.value: night<05:00, ->dusk 06:12, ->day 07:30, day to 17:00, ->dusk 18:36, ->night 20:00; palette step 0.1h; clock poll 15s; ?h= preview
motion.purpose: Relights the scene and switches chrome skin.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Header inset 12->24px, burrow name shown, command pill left-aligned with "get a pet", hint moves bottom-right.

breakpoints.name: portrait
breakpoints.purpose: Scale by width/130, higher horizon, 2 clouds, portrait landmark positions, bottomReserve 130 CSS px.

scaleRules.pixelScale: max(2, landscape ? round(vh/190) : round(vw/130)); width = ceil(vw/S), height = floor(vh/S)
scaleRules.horizon: landscape round(min(92, 0.47H)); portrait round(min(96, 0.27H)); gravelTop = horizon + 17
scaleRules.pondKeepOut: ellipse rx+12, ry+8 around the pond
scaleRules.gravelKeepOut: pets at least 12 px below gravelTop
scaleRules.sprite: 32x32 grid, centre x 16, baseline row 28, feet row 29, 1px pet-ink outline (4-connected)

components.description: Signature: 32px pet, 1px dark-plum outline, top-left light, glinting eyes, blush, feet. Static sketch of the canvas sprite at 4x.

narrative.overview:
burrow is a cozy 16-bit zen garden drawn into one low-resolution canvas and scaled up by a whole number: Mt Fuji behind a forest band, a tiled wall with white plaster lines, a momiji maple, raked gravel, a koi pond, a stone lantern, bushes and moss. The sky is the visitor's own clock. Every scene colour has a day, dusk and night variant, and the garden relights itself by interpolating between them, so the same page reads as noon, sunset or a starry night without a second asset.

The pets are the only things allowed to shout. They are 32 px sprites with a 1 px dark-plum outline, rim light from the upper left, big glinting eyes, blush and tiny feet, and they keep their own fixed tones while the scene darkens around them. Their state is told by pose and props (a laptop, a speech bubble, crumbs, sparkles, a z), never by colour alone, and is restated in a frosted name tag below each stone.

Over the pixels sits a thin layer of modern HTML chrome: frosted pills in Zen Maru Gothic that switch from light to dark with the sky, not with the operating system. Everything is lowercase. The garden is quiet by default and moves in small loops: drifting clouds, koi, falling leaves, fireflies, a flickering lantern, a ripple when a task finishes.
keyCharacteristics: One canvas at about 190 garden pixels tall (landscape) or 130 wide (portrait), integer-scaled with pixelated rendering.
Palette swap, not filters: 35 scene roles, each with day, dusk and night values, interpolated by the hour.
Ordered 4x4 Bayer dithering for every soft transition: sky bands, sun halo, pond depth, lantern glow, contact shadows.
Outlined pets that stay brighter than any scene at any hour.
Frosted, lowercase, rounded chrome that follows the sky.
Deterministic layout: one stepping stone per pet, earlier members never move.

rules.name: The Brighter Pet Rule
rules.body: Pets keep fixed tones and a 1 px `pet-ink` outline at every hour; the scene darkens around them, they never darken with it. A new species gets a base, highlight and shade that out-value the day gravel's neighbourhood and still read against the night.

rules.name: The Palette Swap Rule
rules.body: Every scene colour is a role with exactly three values: day, dusk, night. A new scene element adds a role with all three or reuses one; it never darkens with a CSS filter, an overlay or alpha.

rules.name: The Ordered Dither Rule
rules.body: Soft light in the scene is made of whole pixels on a 4x4 Bayer pattern: sky bands, the sun's halo, pond depth, the lantern glow (full-colour gold pixels, not translucent ones) and the contact shadow under each pet. No smooth gradients, no alpha blending inside the canvas.

rules.name: The Lowercase Rule
rules.body: Interface copy is lowercase, warm and short: names, verbs ("hanging out", "needs you", "asleep"), status ("live", "reconnecting…"), titles ("nobody lives here yet."). Proper product nouns in prose (Claude Code) keep their case.

rules.name: The Mono Means Type-This Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono appears only on strings the visitor would type or paste. It never sets names, labels or headings.

rules.name: The Integer Scale Rule
rules.body: The scene is drawn at logical resolution and scaled by a whole number S = max(2, round(viewport height / 190)) on landscape, or max(2, round(viewport width / 130)) on portrait. Width rounds up (overflow is clipped), height rounds down so the page never scrolls by a pixel. Never scale by a fraction and never smooth: `image-rendering: pixelated` on every canvas, including the 32 px header mark.

rules.name: The Glass Is Chrome Rule
rules.body: Blur, translucency and box shadows exist only on HTML chrome over the canvas. The scene itself is opaque pixels. With reduced transparency the chips fall back to solid `#faf9f5` by day and `#181a20` by night.

rules.name: The Sky-Follows-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Chips switch to their night skin when the scene is night, regardless of the OS theme.

dos: **Do** draw new scene elements into the baked layers with palette roles that have day, dusk and night values.
**Do** keep every pet at a whole-pixel position, inside a 32 px grid, outlined 1 px in `pet-ink`, on its own stepping stone with a dithered contact shadow.
**Do** give each new state a distinct pose and a prop that survives frame 0, plus a lowercase verb for its tag.
**Do** place new landmarks and props outside pet keep-outs, the way bushes and moss already yield to stones and tags.
**Do** make soft light with ordered dithering and full-colour pixels.
**Do** switch chrome with the scene's night flag, and keep chrome as frosted pills with names and titles in Zen Maru Gothic.
**Do** keep ambient motion as small loops gated by reduced motion and paused when hidden.
donts: **Don't** scale the scene by a fraction or let the browser smooth it.
**Don't** darken, tint or blur the canvas with CSS filters, overlays or alpha; swap the palette instead.
**Don't** relight the pets with the clock or let a scene colour out-shine them.
**Don't** use `pet-ink` outlines on scenery; scenery edges use their own `D` roles.
**Don't** put glass, shadows or rounded pills inside the canvas, or pixel art inside the chrome beyond the header mark.
**Don't** give any state other than "needs you" the gold-ringed alert tag.
**Don't** shrink pets or overlap tags to fit more members; grow the garden downward.
**Don't** add underground, soil or dirt scenes.
